subject: Fixing a parameter to zero in multiple group analysis doesn't work as required

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: Fixing a parameter to zero in multiple group analysis doesn't work as required
parts:
I am doing a multiple group analysis in lavaan, and I would like to fix a parameter in one group to zero, but not the other groups. The procedure in the tutorial (https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html) doesn't seem to work when I have three groups and I try to fix a parameter to zero in one group only. I can demonstrate this error in the built-in dataset Demo.twolevel.
First, I create a grouping column to divide the data into three groups:

Demo.twolevel$Groups <- NA
Demo.twolevel[1:833, "Groups"] <- "Group 1"
Demo.twolevel[834:1667, "Groups"] <- "Group 2"
Demo.twolevel[1668:2500, "Groups"] <- "Group 3"  

Then, I create a model with two LV (f1, f2, each with three items). I also add a structural component to the model. I want to fix the loading of y3 on f1 to zero in the third group, while constraining it to equality in the first two groups. 
If you run the code below, you will see in the output that the loading is constrained to equality in the first two groups (as desired), but the loading in the third group is estimated as a free parameter and given a label of "0" (instead of being fixed to zero). Note that removing the quotes from the labels also doesn't solve the problem.  
This problem can also be reproduced in other parts of the model (e.g., if I add a mean structure and I fix the intercept of one group to zero while constraining the other two to equality).  
Is this a possible bug? 

model <- '### Measurement Model
          f1  =~ y1 + y2 + c("a1", "a1", 0)*y3
          f2  =~ y4 + y5 + y6
         
          ### Structural Model
          f1 ~ w1 + w2
          f2 ~ f1'

fit <- sem(model, data = Demo.twolevel, group = "Groups")
summary(fit)

messages.subject: Re: Fixing a parameter to zero in multiple group analysis doesn't work as required
parts: f1  =~ y1 + y2 + c("a1", "a1", 0)*y3

to
     f1  =~ y1 + y2 + c(a1, a1, a2) * y3
     a2 == 0

HTH

Christian

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Fixing a parameter to zero in multiple group analysis doesn't work as required
parts:
Another option is:

f1 =~ y1 + y2 + c(a1, a1, a2)*y3 + c(NA, NA, 0)*y3

So you can have the same rhs term (y3) multiple times with different
modifiers. The first one "c(a1, a1, a2)*" assigns the labels, while the
second one "c(NA, NA, 0)*" assigns the fixed values.

(But you can not mix labels and values within the same modifier; so
c(a1, a2, 0) will not work)

Yves.
